# Worker Agents Skills

This repository bundles the baseline skills installed by [Worker
Agents](https://github.com/agents-dev/workerAgents).

The bundled skills are available under [`skills/`](skills/):

- `mcp-duckgo` — imported from `aahl/skills@mcp-duckgo`.
- `image-search` — imported from `z0gsh1u/oh-my-writing-skill@image-search`.
- `gauntlet-loop` — imported from `robonuggets/gauntlet-loop@gauntlet-loop`.
- `load-sketchfab-threejs` — local asset inspection, normalization, and Three.js/PlayCanvas A/B viewer skill.
- `opencode-zen-completions` — use the OpenCode Zen chat completions API for implementation work.

The original upstream licenses are preserved in
[`third-party-licenses/`](third-party-licenses/).
---
gauntlet-loop
image-search
load-sketchfab-threejs
mcp-duckgo
opencode-zen-completions
---
name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
      issue_number: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    secrets:
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
      OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON }}
      AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ secrets.AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY }}
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with

then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

```js
function taperedCabinGeometry(bw, tw, bl, tl, h) {
  const g = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
  const b = [...], t = [...];
  const pos = [];
  const uv = [];
  const tri = (a,b,c) => { for (const p of [a,b,c]) { pos.push(p[0],p[1],p[2]); uv.push(p[0]*0.2+0.5, p[1]*0.5); } };
  // front (+z)
  tri(b[3], b[2], t[2]); tri(b[3], t[2], t[3]);
  // rear (-z)
  tri(b[1], b[0], t[0]); tri(b[1], t[0], t[1]);
  // right (+x)
  tri(b[2], b[1], t[1]); tri(b[2], t[1], t[2]);
  // left (-x)
  tri(b[0], b[3], t[3]); tri(b[0], t[3], t[0]);
  // top
  tri(t[0], t[1], t[2]); tri(t[0], t[2], t[3]);
  // bottom (not needed)
  g.setAttribute('position', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(pos,3));
  g.setAttribute('uv', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(uv,2));
  g.computeVertexNormals();
  return g;
}
```

## Objective
- Build a polished, mobile-friendly browser game inspired by the title “MadOut 2” (open-world GTA-style driving action), served as a static site from this repo.

## Requirements
- Issue #2 title is exactly `MadOut 2`, with `OpenCode` and `mobile` labels.
- Must work on Android/iOS phones/tablets with responsive layouts, touch controls, and safe-area handling.
- Must be playable in a mobile browser and verified visually in a real browser.
- No explicit feature list was given by the user; scope inferred from the game title and mobile label.

## Decisions
- Build a Three.js open-world driving game titled “MADOUT 2 — BIG CITY LIFE” with procedural city, arcade drift physics, missions, police heat, pickups, on-foot mode/car stealing, synthwave audio, and HUD/minimap.
- Vendored Three.js locally (`vendor/three.module.js`, r169) to avoid CDN dependency.
- Static `index.html` + ES modules, no build step.

Now the car visual. Let's consider adding a few details cheaply. Since all cars share factory, improvements affect traffic too (maybe cost). Draw calls are merged for body/trim/lights, so adding a few merged entries doesn't increase draw calls.

Let's examine buildCarMesh and add:
- wheel arch trim: black boxes above wheels? Since wheels are at x ±W/2, y wheelR, z ±L*0.31. Add dark wheel arch "fender flares" using torus geometry segments? Simpler: four dark boxes around wheel tops. But boxes may look blocky.
- Rear diffuser fins (dark).
- License plate: white-ish box with emissive? Add to lightEntries? Use a separate material maybe. Could add to chrome entries with a plate. But more material = 1 draw call. Keep merged with headMat? A white plate glowing is okay, use headMat (warm white) small box at rear.
- Rear spoiler for sport already.

Maybe more impactful: reshape body using a custom tapered hull. Let's see if we can create a "chamfered box" geometry with rounded edges by using `BoxGeometry` plus vertex rounding? Three.js `ExtrudeGeometry` with bevel is straightforward:

For body side profile in X (width) and Z (length)? Extrude a 2D shape of the car's side silhouette along width. Shape points (z,y) with bevel. Then rotate? ExtrudeGeometry extrudes along +z by default; we want width along x, so shape in (z,y) plane extruded x. We can build shape with x coordinate = z, y = y, then rotate geometry -90° around Y? Let's not.

Alternative: Build a custom body from cross sections along z:
Sections at z = -L/2, -L*0.35, -L*0.1, L*0.15, L*0.4, L/2. At each, define half-width and bottom/top y. Then generate side quads and top/bottom. This gives a tapered body with sloped nose/tail. The top surface can be bodyTop. The cabin sits on top. This is a hull, not boxes. Then add hood/trunk plates, bumpers, skirts, etc.

Would it look better? Likely yes: nose and tail taper in width and height. But the existing car looks like a brick mainly because the body is a constant-width box with flat sides. Tapering front/rear would help a lot.

Let's implement a `hullGeometry` function that takes an array of cross-sections `{z, hw, y0, y1}` and builds side/top/bottom quads with flat normals. But then body paint material is shared with other merged parts. We can merge hull with paintEntries via mergeLocal. The hull has maybe 6 sections * 4 faces = 40 tris, fine.

Define sections for each kind? Generic based on L, W, bodyTop, baseY:
- z=-L/2 (rear): hw=W*0.46, y0=baseY+0.02, y1=bodyTop-0.02
- z=-L*0.42: hw=W*0.50, y0=baseY, y1=bodyTop
- z=-L*0.15: hw=W*0.50, y0=baseY, y1=bodyTop
- z=L*0.1: hw=W*0.50, y0=baseY, y1=bodyTop
- z=L*0.38: hw=W*0.48, y0=baseY+0.01, y1=bodyTop-0.04
- z=L/2: hw=W*0.42, y0=baseY+0.06, y1=bodyTop-0.09
This tapers nose/tail, giving a rounded look. But we also have hood/trunk plates on top at bodyTop; fine. The lower body/upper body boxes would be replaced by this hull. Side skirts and bumpers remain. Need ensure the hull covers cabin bottom etc.

But the hull's flat side may still look boxy; taper helps. Also can add a subtle "shoulder" ridge? Not necessary.

We can create the hull with an elliptical cross-section? For each z, cross-section is a rounded rectangle: top and bottom widths slightly less than mid. E.g., at each section, use 4 points per side? Generate 8 points around the perimeter: bottom center? Actually a car body cross-section is rounded: width varies with y. Could generate 6 points: bottom-left, lower-left (full width), upper-left (slightly narrower), top-left, then mirrored. Then connect rings along z. That yields smooth-ish shading if we compute normals. With flat normals it still looks faceted but better.

Let's write `carHullGeometry(sections)` where each section has z, hw, y0, y1, topScale maybe. For each section, create ring of points around cross-section:
- (0, y0) bottom center? For a closed hull, we need a ring of e.g. 8 points:
  - bottom-left at x=-hw*0.82, y=y0
  - lower-left x=-hw, y=y0+0.08
  - upper-left x=-hw*0.97, y=y1-0.08
  - top-left x=-hw*0.72, y=y1
  - top-right x=+hw*0.72, y=y1
  - upper-right x=+hw*0.97, y=y1-0.08
  - lower-right x=+hw, y=y0+0.08
  - bottom-right x=+hw*0.82, y=y0
- connect consecutive sections with quads for each edge.
- cap front/rear with triangle fan.

But the top surface between top-left and top-right is flat, good. Bottom similarly. This creates a rounded body. However the cabin glass sits on top with a base width W*0.84, while hull top width is W*0.72*2 = W*1.44 vs cabin base 0.84W, okay.

But our existing separate lower/upper boxes and hood/trunk plates would be redundant. We can replace `paintEntries.push(lower box, upper box)` with hull geometry and keep hood/trunk plates maybe at bodyTop+0.02; but hull top already at bodyTop, plates add detail. Fine. The hull y1=bodyTop. The plates sit slightly above.

Need to ensure bumpers at front/rear still align: hull tapers to hw=W*0.42 at nose, while bumper width W*0.98 would stick out wide, looking like a wide bumper on a narrow nose. We should taper bumpers too or keep body less tapered at ends. Maybe use hw at nose = W*0.47, and bumper width W*0.92. Still slightly wider but okay. Or adjust bumpers to W*0.86. Hmm.

Alternatively keep current body but add beveled edges via a "shoulder" strip? Less risk.

Maybe the car is fine for a stylized low-poly game. The city is also low-poly. The screenshot reads as a low-poly GTA. Improving the car might be nice but could risk breaking. Given time, maybe do a modest enhancement: add a tapered hood/trunk by adding wedge geometry at front/rear. We can use `BoxGeometry` scaled? A wedge via custom `wedgeGeometry`.

Let's build a simple wedge for the hood and trunk:
- Hood: a box from z=0.1L to 0.5L, width W*0.9, height 0.12, top slopes down toward front. Use a custom geometry with 8 vertices (top front lower than top rear).
- Trunk: similar at rear, top slopes down toward rear.
This gives a sloped nose/tail, less brick.

But currently the body top is flat and hood/trunk plates are flat. Replacing plates with wedges would create a sloped surface. Let's implement `wedgeBox(w, h, len, slope)` where top front/rear y offset. For hood, front (+z) lower by slope; for trunk, rear (-z) lower by slope. The wedge sits at bodyTop, length L*0.3. This is easy:
```
function wedgeGeometry(w, h, l, frontDrop, backDrop) {
  // 8 vertices: bottom rect y=0, top rect y=h with z-dependent y offset
}
```
Actually a box with top face sloping: bottom at y=0, top at y=h; at z=+l/2 top y = h - frontDrop, at z=-l/2 top y = h - backDrop. Side faces are trapezoids. Generate 6 faces.

Could also make the hood slope start from cabin to nose, but only the plate. The underlying body box still flat at bodyTop, so the wedge sits on top adding volume; the front of wedge is lower than bodyTop, so it would intersect. Need to lower the body top at nose or make wedge extend above bodyTop at rear. Hmm.

Maybe not worth it.

Let's look at the car from the front/side to assess. Screenshot from onfoot shows side: the car has a big flat side, wheels huge, glass black wedge. It actually looks like a low-poly sports car. Could be okay. Let's capture a nicer angle by rotating camera? The game camera follows behind. We can inspect with OrbitControls? Not necessary.

Perhaps more impactful polish: improve lighting/sky, add rain? No.
